title: Importance of Branching Channels for Sustaining Fish Habitat in Riverine Ecosystems
content:
ABSTRACT

Branching channels are recognized for their efficient hydraulic conveyance and the potential to provide extensive floodplain habitats, making them crucial spawning grounds for fish species, such as Schizothorax kolzovi Nikolsky in the upper Yangtze River. To investigate the factors that drive this fish species to select branching channels for spawning, an eco-hydraulic modelling framework was developed. This framework quantitatively assessed the habitat advantages of branching channels across varying flow conditions and compared these findings to those of single-thread channels. Hydrodynamic processes, sediment transport and habitat suitability changes were simulated from 2011 to 2019 in this study. Results revealed that branching channels have diverse hydrodynamic conditions. The riverbed has the resilience to long-term erosion and morphological changes, providing stable physical habitat conditions for spawning. The branching channel consistently showed higher fish habitat suitability than the single-thread channel, with higher weighted usable area (WUA) and overall suitability index (OSI) values, particularly during normal and high-water periods. Over the 10-year simulation period, the riverbed in the branching channel exhibited more stable morphology with less severe deformation compared to the single-thread channel, which experienced significant erosion and sediment loss. The habitat quality in the branching channel remained relatively stable, while the single-thread channel showed a more pronounced decline in fish habitat suitability over time. These findings highlight the ecological importance of preserving branching channels and proving the potential of branching channel designs can also be utilized for river restoration projects.
